newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Crossair sees 12 pct sales rise.
newsitem.headline: Crossair sees 12 pct sales rise.

text.p: Crossair AG, the regional airline subsidiary of the Swissair AG group, said it was budgeting for an approximate 12 percent rise in sales in 1997 to 800 million Swiss francs.
In a letter to shareholders, Crossair's management also repeated that it expects a significant increase in net profit for 1996.
Crossair also said that it expects a slightly higher profit in 1997 based on a significant improvement in operating result but a lack of additional non-operating income.
Crossair already forecast a significant rise in this year's profit in April due to the large expansion programme in connection with taking over routes from Swissair.

"Based on the higher business volume and additional income from the sale of aircraft and aircraft replacement parts, we expect a significantly higher financial annual profit than in 1995," Crossair said.
Crossair reported a 1995 net profit of 17.5 million francs and total revenue of 464.8 million.
Commenting on 1997, Crossair said it expects the weak economy in Europe to continue next year with competition for passengers sharpening further.
Next year will be a time of consolidation for Crossair following two years of strong expansion. An increase in the efficient use of production equipment is the primary goal.
Management has therefore decided on further profit- improvement measures such as optimising aircraft turnaround and better adjusting the seat capacity to market conditions.
Measures to improve the efficiency of pilots and cabin personnel by more than 30 percent have been put in motion and the aim is to reduce unit cost in technical services by 30 percent.

Looking back at 1996, Crossair also said the second half of the year was characterised by an unexpectedly fast and strong rise in kerosene prices. Between July and November prices rose more than 30 percent, which had a negative effect on the profit margin.
Like many other airlines, Crossair raised its official fares on scheduled flights by three percent on December 1.
Negotiations with travel agents are continuing regarding a fuel surcharge for charter flights, Crossair added.
